content.title: How To Wish Someone Happy St Patrick’s Day in Irish - Twinkl Homework Help
content.text: St Patrick’s Day is a brilliant opportunity for you to wish someone a Happy St Patrick’s Day in Irish. This guide will help to teach you some common Irish phrases, as well as explain why saying Happy St Patrick’s Day in Gaelic may confuse someone who is Irish. By the end of the guide, you’ll know just what to say to Irish on St Patrick’s Day. What is the difference between Irish and Gaelic? In Ireland, many people still speak the Irish language. Want to wish someone who is Irish a Happy St Patrick’s Day in Gaelic? They may not be able to understand what you are saying! People often get Gaelic, which is a language native to Scotland, confused with Gaeilge, which is the native language spoken in Ireland! We’ll give you some examples of sayings in Gaeilge (or Irish) below. Sayings in Irish for Happy St Patrick’s Day Below we’ve included our favourite sayings that you can use to say Happy St Patrick’s Day in Irish. How to Wish Someone Happy St Patrick’s Day English: Happy St Patrick’s Day! Irish: Lá Fhéile Pádraig sona duit! Pronounced: Law leh Paw-drig suna ghit ‘Sona’ means ‘happy’ in Irish, and ‘Duit’ means ‘to you’ - so this saying is perfect for when you’re speaking to one person. If you would like to say Happy St Patrick’s Day in Irish to more than one person, you just need to change the ending. English (to more than one person): Happy St Patrick’s Day! Irish: Lá Fhéile Pádraig sona daoibh! Pronounced: Law leh Paw-drig suna yee-uv A Blessing for St Patrick’s Day A more religious way of saying Happy St Patrick’s Day in Irish is to say: “St Patrick’s Day blessings to you”. English: St Patrick’s Day blessings to you! Irish: Beannachtaí na Féile Pádraig dhuit! Pronounced: Ban-ukh-tee nah Fay-leh Paw-drig ghit Beannachtaí means ‘greetings’ or ‘blessings’ in Irish! If you would like to say blessings to many people in Irish for Happy St Patrick’s Day, here is how you say it: English (for more than one person): St Patrick’s Day blessings to youIrish: Beannachtaí na Féile Pádraig oraibhPronounced: Ban-ukh-tee nah Fay-leh Paw-drig ur-iv How To Say Thank You in Irish Now you know how to wish someone Happy St Patrick’s Day, you could learn how to say thank you in Irish if someone wishes you one, too! English: Thank you (the literal translation is: may there be good to you) Irish: Go raibh maith agat. Pronounced: gu ro MAHH aht If you are really thankful, then you can say “may a thousand good things be at you” English: Really thankful (may a thousand good things be at you) Irish: Go raibh míle maith agat Pronounced: Guh RAV mee-lə MAH a-gut How To Say You’re Welcome in Irish A nice saying for when someone says thank you to you in Irish for St Patrick’s Day. English: You’re Welcome Irish: Tá fáilte romhat Pronounced: taw FAWL-cheh ROH-u If you’re saying “you’re welcome” to many people, then the phrase changes a little bit. English (for more than one person): You’re Welcome Irish: Tá fáilte romhaibh Pronounced: taw FAWL-cheh ROH-iv What To Say To Irish On St Patrick’s Day You don’t need to speak in Irish to wish someone a Happy St Patrick’s day. Why not use some of these common Irish sayings as an easier alternative of what to say to Irish on St Patrick’s Day? Why not try out this old Irish blessing? May you have all the happiness and luck that life can hold—and at the end of your rainbows may you find a pot of gold. Or bring a little fortune with this saying? May the best day of your past be the worst day of your future. Another Irish blessing May your blessings outnumber the shamrocks that grow. And may trouble avoid you wherever you go An Irish Saying To Wish Someone Well May the road rise up to meet you. May the wind be always at your back. (This Irish saying means: I hope that you will always find your way easily in life). A Saying About Shamrocks (Otherwise Known as a Clover) For each petal on the shamrock, this brings a wish your way: Good health, good luck, and happiness for today and every day. Now you know how to wish someone a Happy St Patrick’s Day with lots of new sayings, why not write them a St Patrick’s Day card? You could write in the Irish sayings, or perhaps one of the translated English ones, and wish them some good fortune for the year ahead.
